correct_completion: the writer began revising the opening chapter.
full_sentence: Having finished the draft, the writer began revising the opening chapter.
acceptable_variants: the author immediately turned to the opening chapter.
the writer set about revising the first chapter.

options.text: the opening chapter was revised by the writer.
options.why_wrong: The participle 'Having finished' needs the writer as its subject; here the opening chapter becomes the subject, creating a dangling modifier.

options.text: so the revision started right after the deadline.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result that the participle clause does not license, and the sentence never names who finished the draft.

options.text: it was finished by the writer the previous year.
options.why_wrong: This repeats the completion of the draft without moving the sentence on, and 'it' has no clear reference.

options.text: the writer began revising the opening chapter.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with a shared subject ('Having finished ... , the writer ...')
explanation: A participle clause at the start of a sentence must describe the subject of the main clause, so the writer who finished the draft must be the one who begins revising.
translation: Tendo terminado o rascunho, a escritora começou a revisar o capítulo inicial.
